From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>

Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@starlit.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Premium response staircase proposal and regional failover options

Hi Caroline / Raj —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our call, attaching an updated SLA proposal (SLA_Proposal_v2.pdf) that lays out a three-step 'staircase' for premium response and regional failover guarantees. High-level summary: 

- Enterprise Response (Gold): 99.99% availability, 15-min P1 response, 24/7 on-call escalation, regional failover included (EU/US).
- Priority Response (Silver): 99.95% availability, 60-min P1 response (business hours), documented on-call handoff for critical incidents.
- Standard (Bronze): 99.9% availability, 4-hour P1 initial triage, no guaranteed regional failover.

Key commercial notes in the doc: staged credits for hour-by-hour SLA misses, optional on-call retainer (flat monthly) for guaranteed <30min paging during business-critical windows, and a regional failover surcharge for dedicated capacity and cross-region replication.

As next steps, it'd be helpful to understand which pieces are must-have for Starlit and where you see flexibility (credits vs retainer vs availability target). I included a short worksheet in the spreadsheet for tradeoffs (Regional_Failover_Spec.xlsx).

If you prefer, Ben can put together a price band that maps to your estimated monthly committed spend. Happy to set up a 30-min follow-up early next week.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLA_Proposal_v2.pdf (PDF, 6 pages); Regional_Failover_Spec.xlsx (Excel, tradeoff worksheet)

From: Caroline Hughes <caroline@starlit.ai>

Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 10:11:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Premium response staircase proposal and regional failover options

Naomi —

Thanks for the clear summary and the packet. A few quick reactions from our ops + procurement: 

1) EU latency/regional failover is non-negotiable for us — we need failover to EU endpoints within 3 minutes for routing of critical parsing traffic; can you clarify the mechanics behind the "regional failover included" callout? Does that require dedicated reserved capacity in eu-west or a standby warm pool?

2) Credits: our legal team typically prefers a simple uplifted credit (e.g., 10x monthly uptime credits for P1 breaches). The staged hourly model in the draft is more complex; any room to simplify?

3) On-call retainer: we like the concept but need clarity on how it interacts with credits (i.e., do retainer customers still receive credits for missed SLOs?).

4) Pricing: we are still sizing committed spend but expect a mid-six-figure ARR starting Q4. Can Ben share a mid-point price for the Enterprise Response band with and without the regional failover option?

Happy to hop on a quick call — I can include Raj from procurement and our legal rep (agreements@starlit.ai) if we move toward contract language.

—Caroline
Caroline Hughes
Head of Platform Operations
Starlit AI

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Premium response staircase proposal and regional failover options — pricing bands

Hi Caroline / Raj —

Appreciate the questions. Short answers up front, then numbers.

Mechanics of regional failover: we offer two options — (A) reserved EU capacity (dedicated GPU pool in eu-west) for active-active failover, or (B) warm standby with cross-region replication and automated DNS failover. Option A guarantees sub-3min cold-warm failover with committed capacity; Option B achieves ~3–8 minute failover depending on cache warming and routing propagation. Option A is priced as a reserved capacity add-on (percent uplift).

Credits vs retainer: retainer is separate. Customers on an active retainer still receive uptime credits per the SLA; the retainer guarantees prioritized routing, and reduced MTTR through dedicated on-call coverage. Think of the retainer as insurance + operational priority, not a credit replacement.

Pricing bands (mid-point examples, annual commit):
- Enterprise Response (Gold): $375k/yr (includes 99.99% SLA, 24/7 pager, runbook alignment). With reserved EU capacity add-on: $540k/yr.
- Priority Response (Silver): $210k/yr (99.95% SLA, business-hours pager). Reserved EU option: $300k/yr.
- Standard (Bronze): $95k/yr (99.9% SLA, standard support).

Discounting note: for an initial 3-year commit we can offer an additional 8% off list, and volume-based credits if committed tokens exceed threshold X. I put these bands into the HubSpot deal HS-9247; you should see the draft quote there.

If the EU failover requirement is hard, the reserved capacity uplifts are the cleanest path to meet the sub-3min objective. Naomi — if you have a suggested retainer fee that maps to the Gold band, add it to the proposal and we can circulate to their agreements mailbox.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>

Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 7 Aug 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Premium response staircase proposal and regional failover options — operational runbook + escalation matrix

Hi Caroline —

Quick ops note from our side to help make the failover guarantee concrete: we've drafted an incident playbook and escalation matrix that ties to each SLA band. Key excerpts below (full runbook shared via Drive link):

- Detection & Alerting: synthetic traffic monitors in eu-west + active health probes. Failover trigger is a combination of error-rate threshold + regional latency degradation.
- Warm pool warming: for Option B (warm standby) we pre-warm KV caches and maintain a cold snapshot that can heat to operational state in under 5 min; autotuner reduces cold-start by prioritizing top 10 routes.
- Pager routing: Gold -> Redwood on-call engineer (pager), Priority -> CS duty rotation, Standard -> ticket queue.
- Escalation ladder: 0–30m triage, 30–120m remediation plan, 120m+ executive notify + credits evaluation. Credits are computed hourly beyond the first hour, with a 10x cap of monthly fees for cumulative severe breaches.

I called out the execution tasks we'll own vs what we need from Starlit (network ACLs, DNS TTL adjustments, acceptance test endpoints). I've added operational tasks to the Drive runbook: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/drive/SLAs/HS-9247-runbook

If the 3-minute hard SL is mandatory, we should plan for Option A (reserved EU capacity) and run a failover test during contract signoff. I'm happy to schedule a technical dry-run with your infra team.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Customer Success Manager, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Caroline / Raj / Agreements team —

Thanks for the productive back-and-forth. Sounds like we have a convergent path:

1) You confirmed regional failover sub-3min is a must-have — Redwood recommends Option A (reserved EU capacity). Ben's reserved-cap pricing is the baseline.
2) Credits: we'll simplify the staged model to a blended hourly credit with a clear 10x monthly cap (matches your preference for a simpler uplift).
3) Retainer: propose a $6k/month on-call retainer for Gold customers that reduces escalations and guarantees named escalation engineers; retainer does not remove credit eligibility.
4) Operational acceptance testing: Jordan to run a failover dry-run with your infra during the contract signoff week (we'll request specific ACL/DNS changes during that window).

Next steps: Ben to submit a redline-ready quote into HubSpot (HS-9247) by Friday; I will attach the simplified SLA language and DocuSign packet for signatures (DocuSign: https://docusign.com/tx/ABCDEFG). Agreements@starlit.ai — please flag any material edits you want in the SLA; we've tried to keep the credit language simple per your ask.

If that all sounds right I propose we lock a 3-year commit at the reserved EU add-on with the 8% multi-year discount and book the failover dry run in the week following signature.

Thanks again — happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Best regards,
Naomi Feldman
Principal Sales Engineer
